title: GPU compartmentalization: slot-based reservations, SLA hedging, and proactive eviction playbook
creator: Asha Kumar
description:
Background: As Dedicated customers run latency-sensitive workloads we see two classes of tail events: (1) noisy-neighbor spikes that transiently steal bandwidth/SM resources and (2) oversubscription bursts that degrade p95 latency. Existing lane-based soft quotas mitigate average behavior but do not provide predictable throughput hedges for customers with allocated capacity.

Goal: Implement a slot-based GPU compartmentalization layer plus an SLA-hedging policy that preserves throughput guarantees while allowing safe autoscale and cooperative eviction. This ticket covers design, infra prototypes, telemetry, and an operational playbook for proactive eviction when capacity pressure risks SLA violations.

Scope:
- Slot abstraction: contiguous reservation 'slots' on a GPU host that map to tenant throughput contracts (e.g., 2 slots = 8 tokens/s). Slots are lightweight software reservations, not hard hardware partitions.
- SLA hedging: track per-tenant supply/demand and maintain a small buffer (hedge credits) that can be consumed during brief bursts to avoid immediate eviction.
- Proactive eviction playbook: detect pre-failure signals (latency spike + queue growth + cache miss rate) and apply graded mitigations: reclaim hedge credits, throttle best-effort slots, then select low-priority work for eviction with graceful CPU-side requeueing.
- Autoscale coordination: when dedicated pool autoscaler triggers scale-up, the hedging algorithm should delay evictions and favor temporary slot rebalancing to keep critical tenants within SLA.

Non-goals: hardware-level MIG partitioning, permanent hard-slicing across tenants, scheduler rewrite across all clusters (we will implement as an overlay controller at fleet-edge).
design_notes:
High-level design: overlay controller runs in fleet-edge and maintains a soft slot registry. Slots are represented by (host_id, slot_id, capacity_units). The agent monitors three signals: token_service_queue_length, p95_latency, and kernel_sm_utilization. Hedge credits accrue at a rate proportional to underutilized capacity and decay over time. Eviction scoring factors: estimated customer SLA severity, run-time progress, requeue cost, and historical retry success rate. The controller exposes an API for runtime to request temporary slot expansion up to hedge limit.

Data flow: request -> runtime placement -> slot reservation check -> if insufficient, consult hedge -> if hedge available, allow temporary allocation and mark metric; else apply throttling policy. Eviction path uses graceful preemption RPC to worker to checkpoint KV cache ranges and send cancel notice.

Implementation sketch:
- new service: slot-manager (controller + REST gRPC) (prototype in go)
- small runtime hook: allow temporary allocation token + eviction handler (python/c++)
- telemetry: prometheus metrics + tracing spans for slot events
- dashboards: per-pool hedge balance, eviction rate, SLA violations by tenant

Open questions:
- hedging sizing heuristics for mixed-tenant hosts
- acceptable requeue latency budgets for low-priority work
- how to account for KV cache residency when reassigning slots

acceptance_criteria:
- Slot-manager service running in canary cluster and exposing slot registry API.
- Hedging enabled for one dedicated pool with synthetic noisy-neighbor replay and verifies p95 latency improvement >= 30% vs baseline under transient bursts.
- Eviction playbook executed in canary with < 3% false-positive evictions across 48h.
- Dashboards show per-tenant hedge balance, eviction counts, and SLA violation alerts firing correctly.
- Integration tests that simulate autoscaler events demonstrate no data loss during slot reassignments.
- Documentation and runbook added to internal runbooks: Confluence link present.

risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: aggressive hedging may mask true oversubscription and postpone necessary scale-ups. Mitigation: hedge budget limited to 5-10% of pool capacity and integrated with autoscaler budget signals.
Risk: eviction could cause higher application-level retries and customer-visible errors. Mitigation: implement graceful preemption hooks and requeue with exponential backoff; prioritize checkpointing for large KV caches.
Risk: complexity in bookkeeping across controllers. Mitigation: keep slot metadata minimal and store authoritative state in existing fleet store (etcd) with TTLs and reconciliation loop.
rollout_plan:
1) Unit/prototype tests locally and internal demo (week 0-2).
2) Canary A: small non-critical dedicated pool, hedging off, slot-manager observing only (week 3).
3) Canary B: enable hedging with conservative hedge cap (5%), monitor 48-72h (week 4).
4) Canary C: enable proactive eviction for low-priority background tenants only, run 1 week (week 5).
5) Gradual increase of hedge cap to target 10% for eligible pools and add autoscaler integration (week 6-8).
6) Global roll with gradual percentage of pools per region (weeks 9-12).
